items.stem: A circle has diameter 12 cm. Which expression gives its area?
Sofia calculates the area of a circle of radius 3 cm by working out (π × 3)². Explain why this is wrong.
items.answer: Only the radius is squared: A = π × 3² = 9π. (π × 3)² squares π as well.
items.markingKey: B1 only r squared; B1 correct expression. [2]

items.stem: Zara says: "If you double the radius of a circle, its area doubles." Use a circle of radius 6 cm to show that Zara is wrong.
items.answer: r = 6: A = 36π. r = 12: A = 144π, which is 4 times as big. The area depends on r², so doubling r multiplies the area by 4.

items.stem: Explain why π is the same for every circle.
